caption: A quarter-wave vertical is a single upright whip worked against ground radials, which act as the other half of the antenna. On 2 meters, λ = 300 / 146 ≈ 2 m, so λ/4 ≈ 19 inches — which is exactly why the pool says the common 19-inch whip is used on 2 meters: it is a resonant quarter-wave there (T9A08).
spoken: a quarter-wave vertical whip with drooping ground radials, dimensioned as lambda over four, about nineteen inches at one forty-six megahertz
